anatomy.intro: This illustration shows the leafy stems and possible flower spike of a variegated baby rubber plant, not a documented bloom on P31.

parts.function: The broad, cupped blade carries the green and cream pattern.
parts.label: Thick leaf

parts.function: A short stalk attaches the leaf blade to the stem.
parts.label: Petiole

parts.function: Fleshy stems carry successive leaves and give the plant its bushy form.
parts.label: Branching stem

parts.function: Many tiny petal-less flowers crowd onto a slender upright axis.
parts.label: Flower spike

flowers.text: What looks like a narrow tail is an inflorescence: many minute cream-white flowers packed along a spike. NC State describes flowers without petals. Flowering is not yet documented for this collection plant.

growth.note: These species-level stages are not a bloom schedule or a promise that a cutting will retain Bicolor's variegation.

stages.text: An established plant produces new leaves along growing stems.
stages.title: New leafy shoots

stages.text: Additional branches broaden the rounded foliage display.
stages.title: Branching clump

stages.text: Slender spikes can develop without the showy petals of many other houseplants.
stages.title: Flower spikes

habitat.text: The species belongs to tropical America; the named Bicolor cultivar has a horticultural origin. A Veracruz field study records Peperomia obtusifolia growing on trees, on the ground, and on rock across several forest types, including humid and seasonally drier forests. Thick leaves therefore do not make this plant a desert specialist.

lookalikes.name: Rubber plant, Ficus elastica
lookalikes.text: Both have glossy thick leaves, but Ficus forms a woody tree with much larger leathery blades. Peperomia's compact fleshy stems and slender flower spikes distinguish the baby rubber plant; the common name does not indicate close relationship.

mature.text: NC State gives a species range of roughly 6 inches to 2 feet in height and spread. Expect a branching herbaceous plant rather than a woody rubber tree; that range does not establish this cultivar's eventual dimensions indoors.

nameStory.text: The breeder's Obtipan patent names two Peperomia obtusifolia parents. RHS separately accepts Obtipan Bicolor; the green Obtipan patent does not establish this variegated plant's exact origin or patent status.
